title: The HTTP shim gives Swift's own refusals the network's error, so only words tell them apart
evidence: EngineNatives.swift request() answers a request it will not send (its allow-list: "This app does not send that request.", or no token: "Not signed in.") through the same done(0, ..., why) callback a URLSession failure uses, and shim.ts shimFetch rejects every such answer as new TypeError(why). So cloud-adapters.ts eraseFailure (S50b, PR 1751) tells a refusal from a network outage only by matching those words (NATIVE_REFUSALS), and a token refresh's outage only by Swift's "did not answer." (OAuthClient.post's catch, via CloudSync.accessToken). A reworded Swift string would read a refusal as transient and hold Disconnect. Fix: Swift passes a marker (a status text or code) for its own refusals and for a token outage, the shim rejects with its own error name, and eraseFailure reads the name; keep the words as the fallback for builds 11-13, which never send the marker. The same lack of type is a trap (PR 1751 re-check, 2026-11-14): EngineNatives.swift send() passes every URLSession error as words, so a wrong clock (serverCertificateHasBadDate), a Wi-Fi that intercepts TLS (secureConnectionFailed, serverCertificateUntrusted) or cellular data off for the app (dataNotAllowed) reads as no answer, transient, and holds Disconnect while the cause lasts; OAuthClient.post's catch words every token-endpoint error "did not answer." the same way; and a TypeError thrown by our own shim code (ShimBlob, ShimHeaders) or fetchOrFail's body read reads as an outage too. The other way, request()'s own token swap answers "Not signed in." for an offline refresh (a token inside its 60 s early-expiry margin), which reads unknown and lets Disconnect go. Fix with the marker: Swift sends the URLError code; only notConnectedToInternet, networkConnectionLost, timedOut, cannotConnectToHost, cannotFindHost and dnsLookupFailed (owner: dataNotAllowed?) count as no answer; certificate, TLS and ATS errors are unknown; the shim rejects a native network failure with its own error name and noAnswer reads only that.
